explanations: There is no defect. Every accepted message increments inFlight, and accept() pauses the source as soon as inFlight reaches maxInFlight. Each message's process() promise always settles (errors are caught and routed to onFailure, whose own rejection is swallowed), so the .finally() release always runs, decrements inFlight and resumes once it drops to resumeBelow. Messages already delivered after pause() are still counted, so in-flight work cannot grow unchecked, and the constructor rejects a resumeBelow that would make the thresholds overlap.

release() resumes only when paused is true and inFlight <= opts.resumeBelow, which is 16 in worker.ts. Resuming at 63 would toggle pause/resume on every completion; that is exactly what the separate low watermark avoids. It does not wait for zero, and commits play no part in the resume check.

advanceCommit computes the lowest pending offset and commits one below it. When 12 finishes, 10 is still pending, so safe is 9. When 10 finishes, the lowest pending is 11, so safe is 10 and 10 is committed. Committing 12 or 11 would skip over work still in progress, which could lose it on a restart.

process() catches the reserve error and calls onFailure(...).catch(() => undefined), so process() resolves. The .finally() in accept() then calls release(), which decrements inFlight, removes the offset from pendingOffsets and may resume the source. No rejection escapes, so nothing leaks and nothing crashes.
